title: C# 8 to C# 14 feature map (cross-module synthesis)
hook: C# 8 through C# 14 added nullable reference types, records, pattern matching, async streams, collection expressions, and more — spread across the modules you already studied. This topic maps each version to where you learned it and what interviewers still ask.

blocks.text: Language versions are not random feature dumps — they build on earlier modules. C# 8 brought nullable reference types (module 07), ranges, and async streams (module 13). C# 9 brought records and init (modules 04–05). C# 10 brought file-scoped namespaces and global usings (module 01). C# 11 added raw strings and required members. C# 12 collection expressions (module 08). C# 13 params collections. C# 14 refactors field-backed properties and span conversions (modules 04, 17).

blocks.text: Senior interviews ask you to name C# 9 versus 11 features in context — not recite a changelog. Mapping features to modules shows you used them in production: records for DTOs, pattern matching for auth branching (module 11), IAsyncEnumerable for paging (module 13), Span for parsing (module 17).

blocks.title: Pitfalls to avoid
blocks.body: Listing features without tying to a module or use case. Assuming latest LangVersion on an old Target Framework Moniker (TFM) — syntax may compile but APIs may not exist. Confusing C# version with .NET runtime version.

blocks.text: How to prove it in production: interviewers want feature-to-scenario mapping — records for Redis DTOs (module 05), switch expressions for auth branching (module 11), IAsyncEnumerable for SQS paging (module 13), collection expressions for config (module 08), LibraryImport for interop (module 17). When asked 'what's new in C# 12?', answer with OrderDto record + primary constructor, not a bullet list. Cross-link LangVersion syntax to TFM APIs before adopting C# 14 extension members on a netstandard library.

blocks.title: What gets you rejected in interviews
blocks.body: Reciting C# 14 features without tying to a module or scenario. Confusing LangVersion with TFM. Saying you use 'latest' LangVersion in a shipped library consumers cannot rebuild. Listing discriminated unions as TypeScript-only when C# record + switch is the pattern.

interviewTakeaways: Synthesize C# 8–14 as feature → module → scenario — records/DTO, patterns/auth, async/SQS, span/CSV.
LangVersion selects syntax; TFM selects APIs — independent knobs.
Interview answer format: name feature, cite module, give production example — not changelog recitation.
60s: C# 9 records for DTO. C# 11 patterns for auth. C# 13 async streams. C# 14 extensions. Map each to a module you studied.
Follow-up: which C# 11 feature would you use on a ragged CSV import row?
commonPitfalls: Feature list without production example gets you rejected — always tie to module scenario.
LangVersion 14 on netstandard2.0 with APIs that do not exist on that TFM.
Strong answer: 'Records for Redis DTO module 05. Switch auth module 11. IAsyncEnumerable SQS module 13. LangVersion syntax, TFM APIs.'

jsTsCorrelations.note: TS strictness and ECMAScript yearly releases mirror C# LangVersion plus TFM — two axes, not one.
ES2024 syntax in a browser that lacks a builtin is like C# 14 syntax on netstandard2.0 — compiles until you call a missing API. Pin both axes in Directory.Build.props like tsconfig target + lib.
